text:
Aisha Garcia: Heads up — Acme Analytics POC next week. They asked for a network diagram for Redwood Private connectivity: they want to know options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), exact firewall rules to allow, and whether we require any inbound ports. Can we get a short checklist + one-pager they can add to their security questionnaire? cc @Marco Liu @Priya Kapoor

Marco Liu: Short answer: both supported. Longer: prefer VPC peering for lowest latency if there are no CIDR overlaps. Use AWS PrivateLink when you need zero routing changes or when customers require interface endpoints and no peering.

Priya Kapoor: For the POC I usually send a minimal ruleset. Key points: outbound only from customer VPC to Redwood control plane (if using managed control plane) and to model endpoints if routing must go through public subnets. If using Private deployment with VPC-mode control plane, we can keep everything internal.

Tom Reynolds: Security note: we do TLS mutual-auth for any control-plane RPCs? We use mTLS for internal control-plane RPCs in Private; for hosted control plane, we require HTTPS with cert verification. Also include our published set of egress IPs if they need allowlisting.

Aisha Garcia: Can you paste the exact firewall/SG rules you normally hand over? Acme wants port numbers and example CIDRs.

Priya Kapoor: Sure, here's the concise snippet I give customers (AWS example):

```
# Example Security Group / Firewall rules (customer VPC -> Redwood Private)
# Allow outbound to Redwood control plane (managed)
- Protocol: TCP, Ports: 443, Destination: 52.21.34.0/24 (redwood control plane egress list)
# If using PrivateLink (interface endpoints): allow outbound to the ENI's private IP range created by AWS
- Protocol: TCP, Ports: 443, Destination: <interface-endpoint-ENI-cidrs>
# If using VPC peering to a Redwood-hosted private deployment: allow all traffic to peered VPC CIDR or restrict to ports used by service (443, 50051 for grpc if applicable)
- Protocol: TCP, Ports: 443, 50051, Destination: 10.200.0.0/16 (peered Redwood VPC example)
# Health checks and NTP if required
- Protocol: UDP, Ports: 123, Destination: 169.254.169.123 (if using onprem NTP)
```

Marco Liu: Additions:
- If they'll be calling streaming endpoints, ensure the NAT gateway IPs are stable or use egress through a proxy that they can allowlist.
- For peering: update route tables in each subnet to send traffic to peered VPC CIDR; no IGW change needed.

Tom Reynolds: On the questionnaire side, include these answers:
- Q: Do you need inbound ports opened on customer VPC? A: No inbound ports to customer VPC are required for standard operation; all traffic is outbound from customer to Redwood (unless customer requests a private peering arrangement where we route into customer subnets for specific reasons).
- Q: Can you support PrivateLink? A: Yes. We can deploy interface endpoints in the customer's VPC and provide DNS + security guidance.
- Q: Is IP allowlisting supported? A: Yes — we can provide a published list of egress IP ranges or recommend a NAT egress with fixed Elastic IPs.

Ethan Cole: Quick question — if Acme's CIDR overlaps with Redwood staging VPC, what are our options?

Priya Kapoor: Overlap options:
- Best: use PrivateLink (no route table changes or CIDR peering)
- Alternate: use NAT/proxy in customer VPC and route through a non-overlapping transit VPC managed by customer or partner
- Last resort: ask for CIDR remap (painful for customers)

Aisha Garcia: Great — can someone create a one-page PDF we can attach to the SOW and security questionnaire? Needs to be client-friendly and highlight the POC-specific minimal steps + escalation contacts. POC start: Tue 2024-07-30.

Marco Liu: I can draft the one-pager this afternoon. Will include a small diagram (peering vs PrivateLink), bullet rules, sample terraform snippet for PrivateLink endpoint, and an FAQ.

Priya Kapoor: I'll add the exact CIDR examples and the route table commands. For Terraform snippet:
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "rw_privatelink" {
  vpc_id            = var.customer_vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx" # redwood service
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rw_endpoint_sg.id]
}
```

Tom Reynolds: I'll prepare the security QA answers and the list of IP ranges. Note: the IP ranges are rotated quarterly — include a link to the live allowlist we maintain and advise customers to reference DNS-based allowlisting when possible.

redwood-bot: Deploy scheduled: docs/privatenet-onepager draft -> draft-s3://redwood-internal/docs-poc/1719823456-onepager.pdf (for review)

Aisha Garcia: Perfect. Once Marco uploads, I'll attach to the sales deal and send to Acme security. Thanks team :thumbsup:

Marco Liu: Uploaded draft here: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-internal/docs-poc/1719823456-onepager.pdf — feedback welcome, I'll iterate before EOD.

Priya Kapoor: Quick checklist for the POC runbook I'll include:
- Confirm CIDR non-overlap or plan PrivateLink
- Create SG allowing outbound 443 to redwood control plane CIDRs
- Configure route tables for peering (if chosen)
- Provide NAT EIPs for allowlisting (if needed)
- Validate TLS to our control plane & cert fingerprints
- Share contact: infra-ops@redwood.ai for escalation

Tom Reynolds: Also add: rotate credentials step and required audit logging (Flow logs or VPC logs) for the POC window.

Ethan Cole: Thanks all — this is exactly what I needed for the security team. I'll wait for the final PDF and then submit the questionnaire.

Aisha Garcia: Closing the loop: Marco, Priya, Tom — any blockers before I share?

Marco Liu: None from my side.

Priya Kapoor: No blockers.

Tom Reynolds: All good.

Aisha Garcia: Nice work.
